page_title: Atomic Agent: Local AI Agent for Mac, Windows and Linux

sources.entry: Atomic Agent - Local-first CLI and TUI coding agent that runs open-weight models entirely on your machine, with MCP support and 56 built-in tools. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Atomic Agent
summary.one_liner: Open-source, local-first AI agent that runs open-weight models on your own Mac, Windows or Linux machine and drives your browser, files, shell and git.
use_cases: Run a private AI agent that never sends data to the cloud
Automate file organization and renaming in local folders
Clone a repo, read an issue and prepare a fix locally
Run scheduled tasks and send results to Telegram
Research tasks: browse sources, parse PDFs and save notes to memory
Work offline or in air-gapped, compliance-sensitive environments
summary.what_it_does: Atomic Agent takes a task from its desktop app, the terminal or Telegram, then uses a local model on your own hardware to plan next actions. It executes those actions with tools for the browser, files and shell, running some read-only steps in parallel and pausing for approval on risky ones. It loops until the task is done or stopped. It uses llama.cpp to serve the model, GBNF grammars to keep tool calls valid, and a SQLite-backed memory that stores sessions on local disk. The page also describes support for MCP to connect external tools and skills for repeatable workflows.
notable: Grammar-constrained (GBNF) tool calls keep actions structurally valid even with small local models
Claimed GAIA Level 1 benchmark result of 37/53 solved versus Hermes Agent, about 1.6x faster per task (vendor-reported)
MIT-licensed, with a desktop app and a CLI/TUI that can download a local model for you
Supports MCP tool connections and Telegram remote control
caveats: CLI is labeled Developer Preview (v0.6.13); Intel Macs are not currently built
Benchmark comparison is vendor-published and was run by the project itself
Requires local hardware capable of running the model; curated Q4 quants are said to need about 6.7 GB, fp16 about 24 GB
Optional cloud providers such as OpenRouter can be configured, which incurs their token costs
